title: Mellin heat-trace bridge for mixed IR/UV spectral counting
question: Can the mixed IR/UV spectral envelope be converted into a split-time heat-trace and Mellin budget, with UV integrability controlling short times and an explicit IR head controlling the late remainder?
method: For every actual conditional likelihood row, form the normalized intrinsic Laplacian and sort its positive spectrum.
Enumerate all 25 declared IR/UV exponent pairs and every interior split from the R-412 family.
Check the exact finite Mellin truncation identity at tau=1, nonnegative late remainder, and monotonic heat values at seven ordered positive times.
Compare the actual heat trace with the finite mixed lower-envelope sum and the continuous UV integral C_UV alpha_UV Gamma(alpha_UV)t^(-alpha_UV).
Integrate the UV term over [0,tau] and bound the late remainder by the finite lower-envelope modes.
Repeat the full grid in an independent plain-loop implementation and apply omission, sign, exponent, time-order and divergent-tail hostile mutations.
finding: The primary lane passes 212594/212594 assertions over 7 systems, 2688 contexts and 21120 conditional rows. The independent lane passes 149230/149230 on the same grid, the hostile lane passes 8/8, the integrated verifier passes 44/44, and Lean R413 compiles. The inverse trace is [0.44413751605172147,2.0052069566897663], the minimum continuous-UV heat slack is 2.4381603017647795e-05, the minimum short-time budget slack is 0.1831599576706407, and the maximum Mellin identity residual is 1.7763568394002505e-15.
decision_reason: The Mellin identity separates short Euclidean time from the late inverse-spectrum remainder. A sublinear UV exponent makes the continuous heat envelope integrable at zero, while the finite IR/UV lower envelopes bound the late remainder. The result is a concrete uniformity target, not a uniform theorem.

adversarial_review.check: An exact two-mode toy gives a short-time deficit 0.4323323583816936 when the UV term is omitted.
An exact two-mode toy gives a late-remainder deficit 0.3678794411714424 when the IR head is omitted.
Replacing t^(-alpha_UV) by t^(alpha_UV) gives a minimum toy slack -0.56916836825572.
Replacing the reciprocal mode power by a direct alpha power gives a small-spectrum slack -0.04092588658315521.
Reversing the grid creates heat increases 0.38489600036266314 and 1.476288952842503.
Subtracting the late remainder gives residuals 1.2554255560671501 and 0.03827749454306026.
alpha_UV=1 is rejected before an integral budget is formed.
The finite row-wise optimizer and heat grid do not establish uniform constants, a common core, GNS coercivity, a physical gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A closure.

qft_interface.closed: Finite Mellin identity, mixed heat envelope, short-time UV integrability, late finite remainder, full row coverage, hostile shortcut rejection and Lean scalar bookkeeping.
qft_interface.open: Uniform split time and constants on a Hamiltonian common core, phase selection, R-399 shell transfer, R-406 combination, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, continuum and physical-gap obligations.

next_action: Prove a fixed or analytically controlled split time and IR/UV split rule with positive uniform constants on one Hamiltonian common core; transfer the short/late heat budget to the R-399 shell and combine it with the R-406 Schur residual.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite Mellin heat-trace bridge only. It proves no cutoff-, volume-, source-, phase- or exhaustion-uniform estimate, common core, common split rule, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, mass gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A closure.
no_overclaim: The Mellin split identifies a precise time-domain uniformity target and validates the finite implication; it does not supply the missing regulator-independent constants or physical-sector reconstruction.
